root_idea.summary: An uneven or irregular feature in which one part is elevated or thickened while another is depressed or thinned.
root_idea.development: Classical usage also extends the root to measuring or conjecturing quantity or distance and, in a derived verbal construction, tending toward or aiming at something; these developments are not automatically meanings of the Quranic noun.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized noun citation form أَمْتٌ rather than its accusative Quranic surface form أَمْتًا.

senses.definition: An irregularity or unevenness of a surface: a rise, depression, or other deviation from levelness.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic description of the leveled ground, in the construction لَا تَرَى فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا (20:107), it denotes physical unevenness rather than doubt or measurement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To measure, determine, compute, or conjecture a measure, quantity, or distance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use, including estimating the distance between a person and water or computing the number of people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tend or direct oneself toward something; to aim at, seek, intend, or purpose it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I construction taking a thing as the object of one's direction or intention.
A passive Form II construction with بِالشَّرِّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A measure of distance or quantity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in questions or statements asking how great a distance or measure is.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Doubt or uncertainty concerning a matter; disagreement or diversity of opinion about it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions denying doubt or disagreement about a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Absence of indulgence or leniency in a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic interpretation of expressions in which there is no allowance or concession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Laxity, uneven distension, or a crease or depression in a water-skin that is not completely or evenly filled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the irregular surface of a water-skin, including a portion that stands higher than another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fault, defect, imperfection, or blemish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of a mouth, a garment or piece of cloth, and a stone; the lexical use is not limited to any one of these objects.
Used of a journey or pace lacking vigor or steadiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A good way, course, mode, or manner of acting or conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use concerning conduct or a course of action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Suspected of evil or the like.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or participial use related to being regarded with suspicion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A water-skin filled so that it is evenly distended.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a water-skin whose filling has removed unequal laxity or surface depression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water whose distance has been measured or conjectured.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical phrase describing water in relation to an estimated distance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Determined, defined, or definite; known or ascertained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a fixed or definite period and of a thing that is known.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Tend or direct oneself toward something.
Passive Form II construction meaning suspected of evil.
Noun meaning a measure of distance.
Doubt or disagreement, an idiomatic lack of leniency, and the cited weakness branch.
Surface unevenness, including the Quranic use, and water-skin laxity.
Fault or blemish in specified materials or bodily features.
A good way or manner of conduct.
Water described by a computed or conjectured distance.

cautions: The Quranic location is securely supplied by QAC as 20:107; historical citation notation in the lexical evidence is not independently converted into a modern verse reference.
No Mufradat evidence was supplied for this root; the Quranic sense is supported by direct lexical evidence, while the supplied English gloss is contextual only.
